recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-7899 unless FM later chooses a broader editorial rewrite of Claim insurance wording.
issue_request: FHIR-7899 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FM change request asking that Claim.coverage.sequence stop defining the element as a service line item and instead describe coordination-of-benefit processing order.
initial_application: Git commit 15de009ec2f66cf56db34558b702be7d51d32387 explicitly applied Tracker #7899 by changing the old Claim spreadsheet definition from "A service line item." to "Sequence of coverage which serves to provide a link and convey coordination of benefit order." The spreadsheet source was later removed, and later Claim resource work carried the same meaning into the current StructureDefinition.
additional_context: Claim is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The older Claim.coverage backbone has since become Claim.insurance, and source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml defines Claim.insurance.sequence as a number that identifies insurance entries and sequences coverages to convey coordination-of-benefit order. Negative Zulip and Confluence searches found no later community evidence contradicting this source/history conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already satisfies the approved Jira intent and no source edit is needed.

related_jiras.note: The historical application commit mentioned Tracker #7899 and #10590 together, but FHIR-10590 was not needed to decide this seed and was not separately investigated.
